title: Density of solutions for systems of forms: efficient diagonalization for systems of forms of mixed degree (Proposition 2.10)
author: Amichai Lampert
work: Density of solutions for systems of forms
difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is one of the article's three main technical propositions, and its proof is not a qualification exercise. With the whole article supplied as context - the definitions of the Birch rank of a mixed system, of the constants B and delta_m and of the determinantal loci D_m, the geometric lemmas of Section 4 on Taylor expansion, restriction to subspaces and the codimension of the singular locus, and the article's main theorem whose proof consumes this proposition - the author still has to run a source-local argument in two layers. First the auxiliary geometric lemma: compare the two codimension expressions for m and for m-1, use irreducibility of D_{m-1} and D_m to reduce both claims to dense open conditions on the fibre, bound the codimension of the rank-deficient locus S by transporting it to V^m through an explicit linear combination, invoking the Taylor identities to identify the transported equations, and taking a union bound over a projective space. Then the induction on m: verify the base case through the monotonicity lemma, and in the inductive step choose a K-point of the dense open set given by the lemma and apply the inductive hypothesis to the fibre, whose equations have strictly smaller Birch rank. Every step is carried out inside the article's own circle-method-with-Birch-rank framework rather than quoted, which places the unit above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in number theory and algebraic geometry.
